summary.text: Robert Sprague, the Republican Ohio Treasurer of State since January 2019, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Ohio Secretary of State to Allison Russo.
He is a former three-term state representative from Findlay and a former Findlay city auditor and treasurer.

paragraphs.text: Sprague earned a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from Duke University in 1996 and an MBA from the University of North Carolina.
He worked as a management consultant for Ernst & Young and later ran his own consulting firm.
Sprague is from Findlay, Ohio, where he served as city auditor and treasurer.
He was appointed to the Ohio House of Representatives in February 2011 and, after being elected to three terms, represented District 83 until 2018.
He was elected Ohio Treasurer in 2018, defeating Rob Richardson 53% to 47%, and took office on January 14, 2019.

In 2026 he was the Republican nominee for Secretary of State, and his campaign emphasized citizenship checks at registration, photo ID, printed paper ballots, fewer mail-ballot options and making Election Day a state holiday.
He received 46.8% of the vote to Allison Russo's 50.3%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
